articles.title: Bills’ Josh Allen predicted to win MVP after Week 1
articles.summary: Josh Allen’s strong start to the 2026 NFL season has put the Buffalo Bills quarterback in the MVP conversation.
articles.body:
Josh Allen opened the 2026 NFL season with another standout performance for the Buffalo Bills . The quarterback helped Buffalo earn a Week 1 win over the Houston Texans , delivering a big performance in a close game.

Allen completed 20 of 29 passes for 334 yards and two touchdowns, finishing with a 130.5 passer rating. His performance helped the Bills overcome Houston on the road and gave the team an early boost in the AFC.

The season is still young, but Allen has already drawn attention in the race for the NFL's most prestigious individual award. He won the MVP honor in 2024, and his latest performance has renewed discussion about whether he can claim it again.

Russell Wilson predicts Josh Allen to win NFL MVP

Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images

Former NFL quaterback Russell Wilson predicted Josh Allen to win the 2026 NFL MVP award after his impressive Week 1 performance. The prediction puts the Buffalo Bills quarterback among the early names to watch in the award race.

Allen's opening game offered a strong argument for his candidacy. He produced through the air and on the ground, giving the Bills a reliable source of offense in a challenging road matchup.

However, one game does not decide the MVP race. Allen will need to maintain that level of play as the season continues, while other players make their own cases.

Josh Allen and the Bills look to build on Week 1 win

Buffalo will now turn its attention to its Week 2 matchup against the Detroit Lions . Allen's performance against Houston gives the team a positive starting point, but the Bills still have a long season ahead.

The quarterback's ability to make plays as both a passer and runner remains central to Buffalo's offense. If he continues to produce at a high level and helps the Bills keep winning, the MVP conversation is likely to follow him throughout the season.

For now, Russell Wilson has made its early prediction. Allen's next performances will determine how strong that case becomes.

articles.title: Cowboys take brutal hit in NFL power rankings after loss to Giants
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys were expected to fall in NFL power rankings, but this is further than expected. They'll have to come back stronger in Week 2.
articles.body:
When a team wins, they tend to go up in the NFL power rankings, and when they lose, it, of course, goes the other way. That's usually how things work in the NFL, so it should be no shock that the Dallas Cowboys are hurting after their loss to the New York Giants in their season opener.

The Cowboys fell to the Giants by a 28-20 final score during "Sunday Night Football," and it was obviously a frustrating game for Dallas. This team has done a lot over the offseason to beef up its defense, but that just didn't hold on Sunday.

Now, the Cowboys are taking a hit, really a bigger one than you may think, in the NFL power rankings.

Cowboys fall nine spots in NFL power rankings

Now that the NFL's Week 1 roster of games has concluded, Nick Shook of the NFL's official website has released his tally for NFL power rankings ahead of Week 2. For the Cowboys, he took them down in the rankings, which is expected, but they went way down.

Dallas fell nine spots to No. 17. He also has a pretty extensive take on this team.

"The offseason optimism regarding Dallas' defense quickly faded on Sunday night," he says. "The Cowboys were bullied by the Giants' bruising offense and didn't get the one stop they needed most in a one-score loss."

He adds, "It's only one week, but the 'Boys already need to reflect on their shortcomings and work to quickly fix them, or else they'll inspire the same criticisms that followed them to a 7-9-1 finish last season."

It's certainly the case that it's only Week 1, so the Cowboys could absolutely come back from this hiccup. Dak Prescott , CeeDee Lamb , George Pickens and this team is strong. Still, it was nerve-wracking to see this debut.

articles.title: Andy Reid says ESPN's Chris Berman sent him the 90-year-old play that cemented Chiefs' Week 1 blowout of Broncos
articles.summary: Kansas City has run the play before and apparently has "Boomer" to thank.
articles.body:
Kenneth Walker estimated that the film the Kansas City Chiefs watched to prepare for the play that ultimately delivered him his second touchdown and the Denver Broncos a final blow in a 31-10 "Monday Night Football" victory comes from the year 1900.

It actually dates back to 1936, according to Chiefs head coach Andy Reid, who shared postgame that longtime ESPN sportscaster Chris "Boomer" Berman sent it to him.

"We've run it before, just not that smooth," Reid said.

The play took place in the final quarter of the surprisingly lopsided AFC West showdown. Kansas City had the ball on the Broncos' 2-yard line.

Facing first-and-goal, the Chiefs trotted out both Patrick Mahomes and fellow quarterback Justin Fields . They were lined up side-by-side in the backfield, each posing in a three-point stance pre-snap.

The ball was snapped to Mahomes, who veered left with Fields. But instead of pitching the rock to the dual-threat Fields, he shoveled it to Walker.

The reigning Super Bowl MVP ran right, around his offensive line and behind tight end Travis Kelce for the score.

"We worked it over and over in practice, and we felt like that was going to work — and, you know, it did," said Walker, who clocked out with 191 scrimmage yards in his Chiefs debut after spending four seasons with the Seattle Seahawks .

The Chiefs notably ran a variation of the play in a Week 15 road win over the New England Patriots during the 2023 season . That one didn't feature two quarterbacks, though. And Mahomes didn't take the snap. Now-former Chiefs running back Jerick McKinnon did, with Mahomes next to him, and McKinnon popped the ball to wide receiver Rashee Rice .

Rice seemed to bobble it at first before corralling it at his hip while he navigated his way to the end zone.

Mahomes said in the wake of Monday's victory that the play's called "Heisman."

He said offensive line coach Andy Heck ushered the play to the offense but noted, "I'm sure Coach Reid had his imprint as well."

And apparently, if you ask Reid, credit goes to Berman for the inspiration.

Mahomes pointed out that the play could set the stage for more packages with Fields.

"Justin's got a lot of ability, running the ball and throwing the ball as well," Mahomes said. "And, so, hopefully that's just the first iteration of it."

articles.title: Jaguars sign former 2nd round draft pick to boost pass rush
articles.summary: The Jaguars have reportedly signed a former second-round draft pick to boost their pass rush depth.
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars have reportedly made an addition at edge rusher.

According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz, the Jaguars are signing free agent BJ Ojulari .

Ojulari was a second-round pick by Arizona in the 2023 NFL draft. He is still just 24 years old. The Cardinals released Ojulari on Aug. 30 as part of roster cutdowns.

As a rookie in 2023, Ojulari totaled 20 pressures over 161 pass rush snaps. He was a reliable tackler in the run game as well.

Unfortunately, he would miss the 2024 season due to an ACL injury. Last year, Ojulari made his 2025 debut in Week 11, and went on to play 204 total snaps. He logged seven pressures and a sack.

Defensive end BJ Green suffered an elbow injury in the Jaguars' Week 1 game against Cleveland .

articles.title: Lawyers for Victim in Packers Running Back Josh Jacobs' Battery Case File Motion to Seal Evidence
articles.summary: GREEN BAY, Wis. (AP) — Lawyers representing the victim in the battery case involving Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs have filed a motion to seal evidence.
articles.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. (AP) — Lawyers representing the victim in the battery case involving Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs have filed a motion to seal evidence.

"The motion is consistent with our client's desire to protect her privacy, particularly in light of Mr. Jacobs taking responsibility for his actions in the criminal proceeding," Ramses Jalalpour and Amir Tahmassebi said Tuesday in a statement.

ESPN first reported the filing of the motion.

Jacobs pleaded no contest on Thursday to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property stemming from a May altercation with his then-girlfriend.

The woman said Jacobs grabbed her and threw her to the ground as she was trying to exit a garage door, causing her to hit her head. Police said Jacobs also took a phone from her while she was on the ground.

According to a criminal complaint, the woman's statement was corroborated by surveillance video from the camera system in the garage. That video hasn't been released.

In a brief supporting the motion, the woman said she was seeking "to seal and restrict public disclosure of police and supplemental reports, dispatch and communications records, recordings, photographs, witness statements, investigative notes, forensic materials, medical or treatment-related information, digital evidence, and other documents or media."

The brief indicated she wanted "only to prevent unnecessary public disclosure of information that identifies or locates (her), reveals intimate details of the victimization or creates a material risk of further harm to her."

Jacobs was charged in late August and the NFL subsequently placed him on the commissioner's exempt list , which prevents the three-time Pro Bowler from playing or practicing but allows him to keep receiving a paycheck. Players on the commissioner's exempt list are allowed at team facilities for meetings, individual workouts, therapy and rehabilitation and other non-football activities.

After pleading no contest to the battery charge, Jacobs was ordered to pay a $1,000 fine plus court costs. Under an agreement with prosecutors, the criminal damage charge can be dismissed in a year if he fulfills terms that include staying out of trouble, avoiding the victim, submitting to supervision, completing counseling and paying restitution to the victim.

articles.title: 4 overreactions from Week 1 that might stick this season: Woes for Cowboys, Broncos and Patriots, and joy for future Bears fireworks
articles.summary: Dallas' defense doesn't look fixed, and regression may be coming for the Patriots and Broncos after all. As for the Bears, the chase is on for the record boo...
articles.body:
Many will tell you not to overreact on a result from Week 1 's NFL action. Small sample size. It's just one game. Blah, blah, blah.

Let's sideline that line of thinking for a moment and examine what result has staying power through the 2026 season. Brace yourself if you're a fan of the Cowboys, Patriots or Broncos . And keep on dancing if you're down with the Bears .

Here's what caught the eyes of Yahoo Sports writers Jay Busbee, Frank Schwab, Jori Epstein and Eric Edholm, who each answered this question:

What Week 1 overreaction just might stick this season?

Busbee: I'll go with Denver on Monday night utterly failing to put a competitive game together against Kansas City , and not just because it got me guillotined in the first game of the season in a Yahoo Fantasy Death league (Thanks, Jaylen Waddle ). Bo Nix threw an interception three plays into the new season. The Broncos allowed Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker to stomp all over them for 173 rushing yards , including a backbreaking fourth-and-1 that became a 60-yard touchdown.

Most troubling for Denver is the way that head coach Sean Payton condemned every phase of the Broncos' night: "Didn't do a lot well at all in the game … I thought [Kansas City] won, really, in every phase." When one element of a team is misfiring, the others ought to be able to redouble their efforts. When everything goes sideways at once, that hints at deeper, more serious problems.

After the game, player after player insisted that this was not Broncos-style football, but gentlemen — last year was last year. Until you go out and knock around some teams, inconsistency and underachievement IS your brand of football.

Schwab: I'm worried about the Cowboys' defense. Yes, I was one of many who were high on Dallas all offseason. I shouldn't jump ship after one game. But their defense looked no better. The Giants' offense had the best EPA per play in all of the NFL in Week 1, even better than the Bears.

The Cowboys had the same coverage breakdowns due to miscommunication that plagued them last season. That had to be a major point of emphasis all offseason and it still didn't get fixed. They also looked overmatched physically, which is tougher to remedy.

Suddenly there's a realization that new coordinator Christian Parker is doing this for the first time and most of the players Dallas acquired weren't necessarily elite. The most talented player they acquired was safety Caleb Downs , and he's a rookie.

The Cowboys gave up a franchise record in points last season. That won't happen again. But it doesn't mean the defense will be good, either. It's not like the Giants should be some runaway train on offense this season. Count me as very concerned, even after just one game.

Epstein: The Patriots' offensive regression isn't over.

After throwing eight interceptions all of last season, New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye threw a league-high three in a season-opening loss against the Seattle Seahawks . No, I'm not saying Maye will continue his pace for 51 interceptions this year (though that would make for a fascinating story). But I do think the Patriots will hit more bumps on their post-Super Bowl loss road.

Their June 1 trade acquisition, A.J. Brown , showed how effective he can be as a third-down safety valve — before exiting the game with a high ankle sprain that will sideline him at least four weeks. Free-agent signing Romeo Doubs was not on the same page as Maye in the opener, a weakness coming opponents will no doubt look to exploit. Add to all of that the NFL's film on what Maye looks like in coordinator Josh McDaniels' offense, and a far stiffer schedule than last year, and the Patriots don't have the luxury of coasting until Brown returns.

The Pittsburgh Steelers await next, fresh off T.J. Watt 's line-of-scrimmage pick 6. Then come road games at the Jacksonville Jaguars and Buffalo Bills — both of whom swarmed their opening opponents.

Plenty of promise awaits Maye's NFL career. But the danger of Maye feeling he needs to play Superman against teams eager to capitalize on those risks will deal New England more losses soon.

Edholm: The Bears might just have a damned wagon on offense.

Fifty-nine points on the road , with Colston Loveland getting 60 minutes of cardio? Savage.

I think we might have brushed off Ben Johnson's preseason scoring-record bounty as rodomontade. But coaches don't do this kind of thing unless they think they really can pull it off. The record is 606 points, meaning the Bears are nearly a tenth of the way there, with 16 games remaining. Now they need to average only a shade over 34 per game the rest of the way!

The run game is a monster. Caleb Williams is playing like a man ready to blowtorch the league. There's no one weapon you can key on; they have multiple ways to beat you.

I got laughed at on a radio show when I said it, but it's true: The Bears actually could have been more efficient in Week 1. That's a scary thought for the rest of the NFL.

articles.title: Houston Texans legend Andre Johnson criticizes quarterback C.J. Stroud's body language
articles.summary: Andre Johnson appeared on a podcast with Kendrick Perkins and Lil Keke after the Houston Texans' loss to Buffalo and talked about what he's seen from C.J. St...
articles.body:
However, it's going to take time for the Texans quarterback to win back everyone's confidence. For proof of that, look no further than an appearance franchise legend Andre Johnson made on the "LGND TLK" podcast hosted by former NBA player Kendrick Perkins and Houston rapper Lil Keke.

Perkins has long been a Stroud critic , and although the quarterback completed 26-of-38 passes for 274 yards and two touchdowns against the Bills, the Beaumont native and ESPN NBA analyst focused more on Stroud's two fumbles, saying Stroud is not a Super Bowl-winning quarterback.

Johnson put more of the blame for Sunday's loss on the Texans' defense, which gave up 36 points, saying, "any time you're giving up that many points, it's going to be hard to win."

However, the Pro Football Hall of Famer didn't totally exonerate Stroud, who didn't come to an agreement on a new contract during the offseason, willing to play another year under his rookie deal in hopes of playing his way into an ever bigger contract after the season.

After the Texans' defense surrendered a late touchdown to the Bills, the Texans got the ball back at their own 29 with 1:27 remaining. Stroud took his team all the way to the Buffalo 9, but took a sack and then fumbled on another sack on back-to-back plays that ended Houston's final possession.

"When you're betting on yourself and it's time for that contract year and you got that ball in your hands at the end of the game, you've got to go down and score and win the game," Johnson said on the episode that was released Tuesday . "I think when you are in a contract situation and you're in those moments, like you're going against Josh Allen , he's a top quarterback in the NFL. When you're trying to get to that level where you say you want to be (one of) the highest-paid quarterbacks in the NFL. I'm just going to be honest: Who was the best quarterback on the field yesterday? So, when you play and you're in those moments, you've got to live up to what you want. You've got to go out there and show that the money that you want, that you're worth it."

Johnson was more critical of the emotions Stroud shows on the field when things don't go his way, which was especially evident in last season's 28-16 playoff loss to New England when he threw four interceptions in the first half.

"I dislike his body language. His body language is bad," Johnson said. "Any time something happens, it's like… He has bad body language. Me being a former player, your quarterback having that kind of body language is bad because other guys look at you as the quarterback, so when they see you feeling a certain way or your body language is a certain way, it kind of trickles down to the team. I'd say that's the biggest thing that bothers me when I watch the team play."

Despite that, Johnson, who almost always is in attendance for Texans home games, still sounds like a believer in Stroud, who showed better body language Sunday, especially when he scrambled for a big first down and jumped to his feet fired up, which got the crowd even more into the game.

"At the end of the day, talent and all that s- is there," Johnson said. "I'm not going to lie, for me to see him take off running with the ball and jump up and beat his chest, I'm like s- , that's what we need. I thought him doing that was positive. You saw, he got up, hit his chest and the crowd went crazy because you're seeing a different side of C.J. that you've never seen because you've never really seen that from him except maybe since his rookie year. I think for him, the talent and all that s- is right there. It's sitting right there in front of us and we all see it. It's up to him to go out there and make those plays."

In the 68-minute podcast that covers topics throughout the NFL, including former Texans quarterback Deshaun Watson , Johnson didn't reserve his criticisms just for Stroud. When Perkins said the Texans would have gone farther in the playoffs last year if they had Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott , instead of Stroud, Johnson just laughed, adding, "What has Dak won?"

articles.title: Bills’ Josh Allen Predicted to Win Major Award by Former Super Bowl-Winning QB
articles.summary: Josh Allen looked phenomenal in Week 1 for the Buffalo Bills, and if you ask this former star quarterback, a major honor could be coming his way soon. The po...
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills battled their way to a hard-fought 36-31 victory over the Houston Texans in Week 1, and per usual, Josh Allen was leading the way with another dominant performance under center. Allen completed 20 of his 29 passes in the air for 334 yards and two touchdowns, while also rushing for 23 yards and another pair of scores on six carries.

Aside from a risky throw that nearly resulted in a game-ending interception late in the fourth quarter, this was as clean an outing as you could have asked for from Allen. We have seen him star in Buffalo for years now, but with so much on the line in 2026, this was precisely the sort of performance the Bills were looking for from him. If you ask former Super Bowl-winning quarterback Russell Wilson , he believes Allen could be well on his way to winning a major NFL award.

Russell Wilson Predicts Bills' Josh Allen to Win 2026 NFL MVP Award

Over the past few years, Allen has turned himself into arguably the best quarterback in the NFL. He has four Pro Bowl selections and two All-Pro honors to his name, while also winning the 2024 MVP Award. Simply put, anytime Allen is on the field, Buffalo has a shot to win, no matter who its opponent is.

For the most part, Allen was his usual self in 2025, but he found himself getting plagued by turnovers, which ultimately played a big role in the Bills getting bounced from the playoffs by the Denver Broncos . Buffalo spent the offseason loading up again, and in Week 1 at least, Allen was in complete control against one of the best defenses in the league.

Despite all his accomplishments, Allen hasn't been able to lead the Bills on a Super Bowl run yet, but he looked intent on changing that in Week 1. It's only one game, but Wilson believes that Allen knows what is at stake for him and Buffalo, which is why he predicted that he will win the second MVP Award of his career.

"I think that he has a definite chance to win it," Wilson said on "Set Hut!" "I'm calling it out that he's probably gonna win it this year, because I think he knows it's time for the Buffalo Bills. New stadium … new coach. Obviously, the coach has been with him in Joe Brady, but I think it's gonna make a difference this year."

Josh Allen Has His Sights Set on a Bigger Goal Than MVP Win

The individual accolades for Allen are well-deserved, but at this point, he's won pretty much everything you can in that department. The last remaining thing for Allen to do is win a Super Bowl, and while he isn't necessarily approaching the end of his career, it's not a stretch to suggest that he's only going to have a couple more real shots at reaching the top of the proverbial mountain in the NFL.

Buffalo's defense has some things that need to be ironed out, but it will have time to do so, thanks in large part to what Allen is able to do on the other side of the ball. If Allen wins MVP, that'd be great, and the way he played in Week 1 indicates he very well may be capable of doing so. At the end of the day, though, the main goal is to win a Super Bowl, and the Bills will look to take another step towards that goal by beating the Detroit Lions on Thursday Night Football in Week 2.

articles.title: No. 1 overall pick Azzi Fudd ready to hype playoff-bound Wings after season-ending knee surgery
articles.summary: Azzi Fudd is ready to do what she can for the playoff-bound Dallas Wings while rehabbing from arthroscopic knee surgery that ended the rookie season for the...
articles.body:
ARLINGTON, Texas (AP) — Azzi Fudd is ready to do what she can for the playoff-bound Dallas Wings while rehabbing from arthroscopic knee surgery that ended the rookie season for the WNBA's No. 1 overall draft pick .

"I'm going to try to be the best cheerleader I can on the side, the best teammate," Fudd said Tuesday, about three weeks after the procedure. "I'm going to try to be their hype woman."

Fudd averaged 13.1 points in 30 games, the first six off the bench before becoming a full-time starter for the Wings. Her last game was Aug. 5, just two weeks after being the first rookie to win the WNBA All-Star 3-point contest .

"Obviously not how I wanted my season to end. I was definitely a little frustrated at first, but feel like I've handled this one really well, been in a great place mentally," Fudd said. "Just knowing that this was the right decision gave me peace of mind."

Fudd had surgery in Connecticut , where she starred for UConn before becoming the Huskies' second consecutive top overall pick by Dallas. She said she had knee soreness early in the season that initially went away.

"Then it came back up and we tried to manage it, and it wasn't manageable," Fudd said.

The Wings (24-16), who have a four-game winning streak and four games left in the regular season, have already clinched a playoff spot for the first time since 2023. Dallas is home Thursday against Los Angeles for its first game since the FIBA Women's World Cup break.

Reigning WNBA Rookie of the Year Paige Bueckers was the No. 1 pick last year. Bueckers and Fudd won the 2025 national championship together at UConn before Bueckers was drafted by the Wings.

Asked what she was most proud of about her season, Fudd said it was how she felt she handled everything and adjusted to the WNBA, along with her defense.

"Your rookie season is a lot, it's a lot all at once," she said. "Being at UConn, you have lots of alums you get to talk to and pick their brains, but I feel like no matter how much you learn and know before going in, there's nothing that can fully prepare you. So I think it was definitely different coming in and experiencing it and being here for myself."

articles.title: Ex-Seahawks QB Russell Wilson Announces Personal News as Retirement Questions Loom
articles.summary: Seahawks legend Russell Wilson announced personal news as fans have been wondering about how permanent the star's retirement is from the NFL. The post Ex-Sea...
articles.body:
There continues to be questions about the status of Seattle Seahawks legend Russell Wilson , even after the legendary quarterback retired this offseason. Wilson officially began his new media career with CBS Sports debuting on "The NFL Today" pregame show in Week 1.

With Sam Darnold sidelined with a glute injury, there has been some chatter on social media that perhaps the Seahawks could make a call to Wilson. Yet, it is pretty clear that Wilson has moved on and remains focused on his new career venture.

In addition to his weekly appearance on CBS, Wilson just announced the launch of a new weekly YouTube show called "Set, Hut!" with former NFL offensive lineman Kyle Long .

"Crazy Week 1 in the @NFL," Wilson noted in a September 14, message on X. "See you on me & @Ky1eLong new show! "Set, Hut!" Live Tomorrow 2pm Eastern on @YouTube."

So, how did Wilson perform in his media debut? Let us know in the comments.

Seahawks News: Russell Wilson Went Viral for Predicting That Broncos QB Joe Burrow Will Demand a Trade

There have been some valid concerns about Wilson's viability as a media personality given his somewhat robotic press conferences as a player. It appears Wilson may have been saving up his takes for his post-retirement career.

Wilson came out firing during his regular-season debut. The Seahawks legend went viral for predicting that Cincinnati Bengals star quarterback Joe Burrow will demand a trade.

"I think he's tired of losing," Wilson remarked on Burrow during a September 13, edition of CBS' "NFL Today." "He said that a few times.

"He's really focused on making sure that this is that special year. And listen, if it doesn't go well in Cincinnati this year, I'm just saying," Wilson added.

"I'm just telling you right now. … I'm telling you right now, if it doesn't go well in Cincinnati this year, Joe Burrow's gone. I think he wants to leave and what's gonna be interesting is where does he go? There's some great teams that need a quarterback."

Russell Wilson's NFL Career Is Largely Defined by Seahawks Tenure

It was an ugly breakup between the Seahawks and Wilson, but as time goes on, it is almost a certainty that the quarterback's career will largely be associated with Seattle. Wilson struggled in all of his next stops after the Seahawks traded the quarterback.

Additionally, the Seahawks were able to build a second Super Bowl roster partly as a result of the blockbuster deal with the Denver Broncos .

Is Russell Wilson Good as an NFL Media Analyst?

It is too early to tell how Wilson's new career as a media analyst will go. At the very least, Wilson proved relevant with his Burrow take going viral.

Wilson and Long's new show will add a new data point to the former NFL quarterback's media evaluation.

"The network announced Set, Hut!, a new weekly series hosted by the two NFL Today analysts, premiering Tuesday, Sept. 15 at 2 p.m. ET," Awful Announcing's Sam Neumann detailed in a September 14, article titled, "CBS Sports launches new digital series with Russell Wilson, Kyle Long."

"The show will stream live on the NFL on CBS YouTube channel, with episodes also available on Paramount+, CBS Sports HQ, and podcast platforms," Neumann added.

"Per CBS, Set, Hut! will feature guest interviews, insight and analysis on the league's biggest topics, and real-time interaction with fans."

articles.title: Best Fantasy Football Waiver Wire Pickups After Week 1
articles.summary: Need help attacking the waiver wire ahead of Week 2? Click here for The Sporting News' waiver wire report.
articles.body:
Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season gave fantasy football managers plenty of surprises, and now it's time to hit the waiver wire.

While it's important not to overreact to one game, several players emerged with the kind of workload and opportunity that could translate into legitimate season-long fantasy value. Whether you're looking for an immediate starter, an injury replacement or a player who could develop into a weekly option, there are several names worth targeting before Week 2.

Here are the best fantasy football waiver wire pickups following Week 1.

Week 1 fantasy waiver wire: best pickups

Coker is one of the most intriguing wide receiver additions after Week 1. The Panthers rookie caught eight passes for 138 yards and two touchdowns, while playing 84% of Carolina's offensive snaps. His combination of playing time, targets, and production makes him much more than a one-week flier.

Bryce Young also threw for 361 yards and four touchdowns in Carolina's 59-37 loss to Chicago , giving Coker an appealing quarterback situation for fantasy purposes.

Coker should be one of the highest-priority waiver claims in most leagues.

Black's Week 1 performance deserves attention, particularly because he wasn't simply a change-of-pace option behind Christian McCaffrey .

Black split work with McCaffrey and finished with 70 total yards, showing that San Francisco could have a legitimate role for him alongside its star running back.

Managers shouldn't expect McCaffrey's workload to disappear, but Black's involvement makes him an intriguing bench addition with standalone value and significant upside if his role grows.

Shough was one of the biggest quarterback surprises of Week 1. The Saints quarterback threw for 410 yards and three touchdowns, immediately putting himself on the fantasy radar.

Quarterback is typically deep enough that managers don't need to rush to add every surprise performer, but Shough is worth a roster spot in leagues where a streaming option or quarterback depth is needed.

His passing volume gives him a realistic path to fantasy relevance beyond a single big performance.

Tight end is once again a difficult position to navigate on the waiver wire, which makes Gesicki particularly interesting.

Gesicki led Cincinnati in receptions in Week 1 and emerged as a reliable target for Joe Burrow .

Managers searching for help at tight end shouldn't overlook a player who is already seeing meaningful involvement in a strong passing offense.

Wicks also deserves consideration after stepping into a much larger role in Philadelphia .

He played 91% of the Eagles' offensive snaps and finished Week 1 with 78 receiving yards and a touchdown.

The playing time is especially encouraging. Wicks isn't simply a player who happened to score a touchdown; he was on the field consistently enough to potentially maintain fantasy value.

Boston is another young receiver fantasy managers should monitor closely.

The Browns rookie led Cleveland in receiving snaps and scored a touchdown in Week 1. While some of his production came late in the game, his role makes him an intriguing stash for managers with deeper benches.

He may not immediately be a weekly starter, but Boston has enough opportunity to justify a waiver claim in deeper leagues.

Mayer becomes especially interesting because of Brock Bowers ' knee injury. Bowers is expected to miss time after undergoing a procedure, leaving Mayer with an opportunity to take on a significantly larger role in the Raiders' offense.

Mayer previously showed that he can provide fantasy production when Bowers is unavailable, making him one of the more obvious tight-end replacements for fantasy managers dealing with the Bowers situation.

Vele is another wide receiver worth adding, particularly in deeper leagues.

His emergence gives fantasy managers another young receiver to monitor as Denver 's offense develops. Several Week 2 waiver-wire analysts have identified Vele as a player whose role could continue to grow following the opening week.

articles.title: Browns’ KC Concepcion’s Reaction to Denzel Boston’s First TD Says it All About Their Friendship
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns don’t have many positive takeaways from their Week 1 outing against the Jacksonville Jaguars, but rookie wide receiver Denzel Boston gav...
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns don't have many positive takeaways from their Week 1 outing against the Jacksonville Jaguars , but rookie wide receiver Denzel Boston gave his team's fans — and fellow rookie wideout KC Concepcion — something to feel good about.

Boston, who was taken by the Browns in the second round as the 39th pick overall in the 2026 NFL Draft, scored Cleveland's only touchdown in what turned out to be a 34-10 loss to the Jaguars at EverBank Stadium in Jacksonville. It happened with just under two minutes left in the fourth quarter and with the game already out of Cleveland's reach. On a 2nd-and-5 at the Jags' 46, Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson loaded up for a long throw and found Boston right in the end zone for the score.

Browns Wide Receiver Concepcion Reacts to Fellow Rookie's TD in Week 1

"Man, I was so excited for my dog," Concepcion said about Boston's touchdown ( via Spencer German of 92.3 The Fan ).

"Y'all go back and watch the film. As soon as I saw him catch it, you know, I was the first guy down there, you know, cheering him off. You know, me and Denzel, you know, we came in together, you know, and that's my brother, you know. You know, I love to see him win and, you know, whenever we score, you know, I was very, very excited for him."

Concepcion, drafted in the first round (24th overall) of this year's draft, actually started the drive where Boston scored the touchdown. The former Texas A&M Aggies star rushed for 10 yards in the first play of the series.

Overall, Boston had 59 receiving yards and a touchdown on two catches and four targets.

Meanwhile, Concepcion recorded 43 receiving yards with zero touchdowns on four catches and a team-leading five targets, in addition to his 15 rushing yards on three carries.

Perhaps Concepcion will finally get his first touchdown in the NFL in Week 2, when the Browns visit the Tampa Bay Buccaneers .

articles.title: Lions Take Another Major Hit As Key Name Joins Growing Injury List
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions don’t have much time to enjoy their dramatic 31-30 overtime victory over the Buffalo Bills in Week 1 of the NFL season, as they immediately...
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions don't have much time to enjoy their dramatic 31-30 overtime victory over the Buffalo Bills in Week 1 of the NFL season, as they immediately began preparations for a Thursday night matchup against the Buffalo Bills in Week 2.

The Lions, who were shorthanded against the Saints , were even more so this week at practice, as offensive tackle Blake Miller, Detroit's first selection in the 2026 NFL Draft, missed Monday's practice.

Not only was Miller unavailable for Detroit's walkthrough on Tuesday, but the Lions also added a new name to the Injured List, sparking more concern.

The Detroit Lions Have Added Cornerback DJ Reed

The Lions have added cornerback DJ Reed to their injured list with a foot injury, according to the latest report released.

Additionally, Christian Mahogany , who departed Sunday's game and missed Monday's practice, was also unavailable on Tuesday.

Reed is in his second season with the Lions after signing a three-year contract prior to last season; he was limited to eight games in 2025.

DJ Reed Is Entering His Second Year With The Lions

Reed was taken by the San Francisco 49ers in the fifth round (142nd overall pick) of the 2018 NFL Draft out of Kansas State; he also attended Cerritos and Fresno State.

He started his career contributing primarily on special teams while also seeing snaps at cornerback, nickel and safety. He made two starts as a rookie and finished with 41 tackles, a sack and a forced fumble across 15 games.

His role remained limited in 2019, though he appeared in all 16 games and scored his first NFL touchdown on a fumble return against Arizona . Reed also saw limited action during San Francisco 's run to Super Bowl LIV.

Reed's 2020 season got off to a difficult start when he suffered a torn pectoral muscle while lifting weights during the offseason. San Francisco subsequently waived him with a non-football injury designation.

Seattle claimed Reed off waivers in August 2020, though a surgically repaired torn pectoral kept him sidelined until Week 8. He immediately stepped into a significant role, starting at nickel and later taking over as an outside cornerback.

Reed made an immediate impact in his Seattle debut against San Francisco, recording six tackles and his first career interception. He eventually secured a starting job for the remainder of the season and finished with 62 tackles, seven pass breakups and two interceptions in 10 games, including eight starts.

Reed remained a full-time starter with the Jets , posting 76 tackles, nine pass breakups and an interception in 2023. Injuries limited him to 14 starts the following season, when he recorded 64 tackles, 11 pass deflections and a sack. He then signed with the Lions in 2025, but was limited to just eight games.

articles.title: Chiefs Rookie CB Mansoor Delane Faces MRI After Right Shoulder Injury
articles.summary: Mansoor Delane barely had time to settle into his first NFL game before his night took a turn. The Kansas City Chiefs’ rookie cornerback opened his career wi...
articles.body:
Mansoor Delane barely had time to settle into his first NFL game before his night took a turn. The Kansas City Chiefs' rookie cornerback opened his career with an interception of the Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix , then left the game after landing awkwardly on his right shoulder.

Now the Chiefs are waiting on more information. Delane is set to undergo an MRI on Tuesday after X-rays came back negative, according to NFL Network's Mike Garafolo. The early hope is that the sixth overall pick suffered a sprain rather than another major shoulder issue.

Mansoor Delane's Shoulder MRI Could Determine His Early Role With The Kansas City Chiefs

Delane's NFL debut could hardly have started better. On just his third defensive snap, he picked off Nix and gave the Chiefs an early takeaway. He stumbled after making the interception and landed on his right shoulder during the return.

Head coach Andy Reid did not have much to offer after the game.

"We're just gonna see where that goes from here."

That ended up being his only major moment of the night. Delane was ruled questionable to return before heading to the locker room. The Chiefs later confirmed he would not come back, leaving Kristian Fulton to take over his spot in the secondary.

The latest report from Garafolo provides a little more optimism. The X-rays showed that Delane's shoulder is stable, while the MRI is expected to give the Chiefs a clearer idea of the injury and his potential recovery timeline.

There is some added concern because this is not the first time Delane has dealt with trouble in that shoulder. The rookie missed time during OTAs and mandatory minicamp and was also sidelined early in training camp before returning during the preseason.

That history makes Tuesday's MRI particularly important. Former NFL team doctor David J. Chao also looked at video of the play and suggested Delane could be dealing with a right AC joint sprain. Chao noted that the rookie who went to the locker room, however, could potentially have returned with an injection. However, that was only an assessment from video, and the MRI remains the test that should provide the real answer.

The Chiefs made a major investment in Delane for a reason. The Chiefs moved up to No. 6 in the 2026 NFL Draft to select the LSU cornerback, expecting him to become an important piece of Steve Spagnuolo's defense.

Losing him for an extended stretch would create an immediate problem in a secondary that already has plenty riding on its younger players. Fulton is an obvious option for more snaps, while Kansas City also has rookies such as Jadon Canady and Christian Roland-Wallace available.

For now, there is no confirmed timetable. The Chiefs will have to wait for the MRI before deciding what Delane's status looks like for Week 2 against the Indianapolis Colts .

articles.title: NFL Preseason Catch Leader Rivaldo Fairweather Gets Commanders Look After Surprising Exit
articles.summary: Rivaldo Fairweather is getting another NFL opportunity after a preseason that put his name on the radar. The former Arizona Cardinals and Dallas Cowboys tigh...
articles.body:
Rivaldo Fairweather is getting another NFL opportunity after a preseason that put his name on the radar. The former Arizona Cardinals and Dallas Cowboys tight end is working out for the Washington Commanders .

Fairweather's timing is interesting because he has already been moving around since the preseason ended. He worked out for the Kansas City Chiefs on September 4 and was also scheduled to visit the Indianapolis Colts . Now the Commanders are taking a look at the tight end who led the NFL in preseason catches.

Rivaldo Fairweather Gets Another Shot With The Washington Commanders

Fairweather caught 17 of 21 passes for 150 yards during the preseason, making his eventual release by the Cardinals a bit of a surprise. He had been active in the passing game throughout the summer and finished with more receptions than any other player in the league during the preseason.

The production wasn't random. Fairweather went unselected in the 2025 NFL Draft following his stint as a collegiate player at Auburn. Fairweather originally signed with the Cowboys and had 5 receptions for a touchdown in the 2025 preseason. Dallas didn't keep Fairweather on the first 53-man roster and kept him on the practice squad.

The Cardinals subsequently signed Fairweather from the Dallas practice squad in December. Fairweather is going into this year's preseason fight to make the roster and made a convincing case for himself in doing so. His 17 receptions came on 21 targets, while his 150 yards receiving gives teams a lot of recent film to look at.

Still, the Cardinals moved on. That has left Fairweather looking for a place where his receiving ability can turn into a regular-season opportunity. So far, teams have continued to show interest.

The Chiefs were one of the first clubs to bring him in after Arizona's roster decision. Kansas City was looking for additional tight end depth, and Fairweather's size and receiving production made him an obvious player to examine. The Colts also showed interest, particularly after losing Will Mallory to injured reserve and being left with only three tight ends on the active roster.

Now Washington has joined the list. Fairweather stands around 6-foot-4 and 252 pounds, giving him the size teams generally want from the position. He also has some experience working from the slot. His final two college seasons produced 69 catches for 766 yards and 8 touchdowns.

The Commanders don't necessarily need the 24-year-old to walk in and become a major part of the offense. A workout is simply a chance for the team to see where he is physically and whether his preseason production translates to what Washington wants from its tight ends.

For Fairweather, though, the opportunit y is bigger. The Commanders are now the latest team willing to take a closer look. If Fairweather can impress during the workout, his unusual preseason exit could quickly turn into another chance on an NFL roster.

articles.title: How Sean Payton’s Secret Drew Brees Comeback Plan to Replace Bo Nix Fell Apart
articles.summary: Bo Nix fractured his ankle late last season as the Denver Broncos were pushing toward the AFC Championship, and the franchise was suddenly scrambling for ans...
articles.body:
Bo Nix fractured his ankle late last season as the Denver Broncos were pushing toward the AFC Championship, and the franchise was suddenly scrambling for answers at quarterback. What happened next is only coming to light now.

A pair of Broncos assistant coaches secretly reached out to Drew Brees about coming out of retirement to play in the AFC title game, and Brees actually worked out before a wrist issue shut the plan down entirely.

Drew Brees workout ended Broncos' postseason comeback plan

Nix went down on the second-to-last play of Denver's divisional round overtime win over the Buffalo Bills on January 17, fracturing his ankle and ending his season on the spot. Two days earlier, Brees had turned 47 years old.

That did not stop then-offensive coordinator Joe Lombardi and offensive assistant Pete Carmichael, both longtime Brees coaches from their days together in New Orleans , from picking up the phone.

Feb 5, 2026; San Franciso, CA, USA; Drew Brees during a press conference introducing the NFL Hall of Fame Class of 2026 at Palace of Fine Arts. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images

"Well, Scott, here's the untold story behind Bo Nix's fractured ankle. A couple days after that injury happened, the then Broncos assistant coaches Pete Carmichael and Joel Lombardi privately reached out to Drew Brees to gauge his interest in coming in that week, playing for the team, and potentially playing in the AFC Championship game," insider Adam Schefter said on ESPN.

Brees told them he wanted to work out first to see how his body responded. When he did, his wrist was bothering him, and that was the end of it. Had he felt good, Schefter reported, Payton would have signed him and chosen between Brees and backup Jarrett Stidham to start against the New England Patriots .

The entire pursuit happened without Sean Payton's knowledge. Lombardi and Carmichael wanted to gauge Brees' interest before bringing it to the head coach. When Payton eventually found out during the offseason, he initially thought his assistants were talking about the 2021 situation in New Orleans, when injuries and COVID absences forced the Saints to start Ian Book on a Monday night against the Dolphins after the team had briefly approached Brees about returning then too.

Had Brees suited up, he would have been 47 years old and five years removed from his last NFL game, a playoff loss to Tom Brady and the Buccaneers in January 2021. It would have made him the second-oldest quarterback to play in an NFL game in history, behind only George Blanda, who appeared in a game at 48. Instead, Stidham started the AFC Championship, completed 17 of 31 passes for 133 yards and a touchdown, and the Broncos came up short against the Patriots after a critical fumble on an attempted throwaway that was ruled a backwards pass.

Brees had previously hinted on the New Heights podcast with Travis and Jason Kelce that he had an opportunity to return but did not share the team or details. The Schefter report fills in the blanks.

Sean Payton now moves forward with Bo Nix in Denver

Payton has since moved on and made clear that Nix remains his guy heading into 2026. He recently defended the young quarterback publicly against outside criticism, a sign of how much confidence Denver's coaching staff still has in him after his strong start to his NFL career.

Jarrett Stidham has been named the backup again this season, a role that took on far more importance than anyone expected a year ago. The Broncos will hope the quarterback room stays quiet in 2026.

Brees, meanwhile, was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in August and has settled into a role as a game analyst at Fox Sports. His near-comeback will go down as one of the more remarkable what-ifs in recent NFL history.

articles.title: Simone Biles built a custom $3 million waterfront mansion in Texas; after years of planning and delays, the Olympian settled into the lakefront estate following a prior $1.1 million property buy
articles.summary: International Sports News: Simone Biles and her husband Jonathan Owens have finally moved into the Texas home they spent years planning and building. The custom lakefront mansio.
articles.body: Simone Biles and her husband Jonathan Owens have finally moved into the Texas home they spent years planning and building. The custom lakefront mansion near Houston was completed on November 11, 2025, after the couple began working on its design in 2020. The project took much longer than they first expected, with Biles sharing updates as the house slowly took shape. The seven-time Olympic medalist and Owens chose to build the home from the ground up instead of buying a finished property. The result is a large lakefront house with spaces designed around their everyday life, pets and love of sports.When did Simone Biles and Jonathan Owens start building their Texas mansionThe story of Simone Biles and Jonathan Owens’ new home began in 2020, when they started planning the property. Biles later explained that simply getting the design ready took about a year.The next wait came from the homeowners association. According to Biles, the required approvals took time, which pushed the actual start of construction to February 2022.That meant the couple had already spent a long time thinking about the house before construction even began. Once work started, Biles continued to share photos and videos showing the property at different stages, from the early framework to the finished rooms.The house was expected to take far less time. After years of waiting, Biles summed up her frustration in a short Instagram update: "They lied when they said nine months to build!"She also shared the timeline behind the project, writing: "Home building requires a lot of patience."Biles later explained: "Started the design process in 2020 and took a year to complete," before adding, "Approvals took a while from [the] HOA; broke ground in Feb 2022; completed 11/11/25."The project therefore stretched across several major moments in the couple's lives. They got married in 2023, while Biles also returned to competition and competed at the Paris Olympics in 2024.What is inside Simone Biles and Jonathan Owens’ $3 million lakefront homeThe home was built around a mix of comfort, entertainment and spaces that fit the couple's interests. The property has been widely estimated at around $3 million, although the exact final cost has not been publicly confirmed.One of the main features is the kitchen. It has two large islands, custom cabinets and black-and-white marble details. Large glass doors also connect the living areas with the outdoor space and lake views.The house also has a primary bathroom with a large marble finish, two sinks and a spacious shower. There is a game room, home theater and wet bar, giving the couple several areas to spend time at home.Sports are also part of the property. The outdoor area includes a swimming pool and spa beside the lake, along with a basketball court. An in-ground trampoline has also been built close to the water.The house has several personal touches that make it different from a standard luxury property. Biles and Owens have a separate room for their dogs, complete with a pet spa area and built-in feeding space. The room uses the same black-and-white look seen in other parts of the house.The laundry room is another detail Biles has highlighted. Instead of sharing one set of machines, the couple have separate washers and dryers.Biles joked about the reason behind that decision, writing: "Since Jonathan always wants to do laundry the exact same day as me," and then adding, "Now [there is] one set for each of us."How did Simone Biles’ earlier $1.1 million Texas property compare with the new mansionBefore the lakefront house was completed, Biles already had a Texas home where she and Owens spent time during the construction period.Realtor.com reported in 2024 that Biles bought the contemporary Spring, Texas, property in 2020. The 4,000-square-foot home has four bedrooms and 3.5 bathrooms and sits on just over an acre.The property had been listed for $863,500 in 2020, but the exact amount Biles paid was not publicly confirmed. That makes the often-repeated $1.1 million purchase figure difficult to verify.The earlier home also had several features that suited Biles' lifestyle, including a large kitchen, open living areas, a primary suite and a mud room with a pet-washing and feeding area.It also appeared in the Netflix documentary series “Simone Biles Rising,” which followed the gymnast's life and return to elite competition.The new lakefront property is a different kind of home. Rather than taking an existing house and adapting it, Biles and Owens had the chance to decide what they wanted from the beginning. That included the layout, sports areas, pet space and entertainment rooms.When did Simone Biles and Jonathan Owens finally move into the new Texas homeThe house was officially completed in November 2025, but the couple did not immediately settle into it full time.At the time, Owens was playing for the Chicago Bears, meaning the couple spent part of their time in Chicago. After the NFL season ended, Biles began sharing more pictures from the Texas property as the couple started making the house their home.In February 2026, Biles showed more of the finished interiors, including her closet and office area. The couple had also returned to Texas after their time in Chicago.Architectural Digest reported that Biles had followed the project closely for about five years, documenting the transformation from an unfinished structure into the completed lakefront home.The long wait finally gave the couple a house built around their own needs rather than a property they had simply purchased and moved into.Biles' latest home also comes at a different stage of her life. She has already competed in three Olympic Games and remains one of the most decorated gymnasts in history. Owens' NFL career has also taken the couple to different cities.For now, their custom Texas house gives them a home base that was designed by them from the start. In 2026, Biles also said she planned to spend time in Indianapolis to support Owens after he joined the Colts, so the Texas property is not necessarily where the couple will spend every month of the year. Still, after five years of planning, waiting and construction, the lakefront home has finally become part of their lives.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Justin Herbert did not seem too pleased with the Chargers after disastrous loss to Arizona Cardinals
articles.summary: Justin Herbert's terse postgame answers and alarming sack totals raised new concerns after the Los Angeles Chargers' lopsided loss to Arizona.
articles.body: The Los Angeles Chargers under Jim Harbaugh have been remarkably consistent. In 2024, they finished 11-6 and in second place in the AFC West, only to lose 32-12 to the Houston Texans in the Wild Card round of the NFL playoffs. In 2025, they finished ... 11-6 and in second place in the AFC West. They then promptly lost in the Wild Card round 16-3 to the New England Patriots. While the Chargers' defense improved immediately under Harbaugh and defensive coordinator Jesse Minter, there's been a sense that the offense was not living up to its potential. Quarterback Justin Herbert has the traits to succeed in the modern NFL, elite arm strength and the ability to keep defenses honest by moving out of the pocket and scrambling when plays break down. NFL WEEK 1 PROPER REACTIONS: RAMS PANIC, BEARS HYPE AND CHARGERS DOUBTS NEED PATIENCE AFTER ONE GAME Offensive line play and injuries have slowed the Chargers' attack down, however, and they scored just 368 points in 2025, well behind the league-leading Rams with 518. Harbaugh hoped to address some of those issues by bringing in former Miami Dolphins head coach Mike McDaniel to run the offense. The first opportunity to see that new-look Chargers scheme in action though, was a disaster. Putting it mildly. Los Angeles entered their season opener at SoFi Stadium as significant favorites over the Arizona Cardinals, coming off a dismal 3-14 season that saw them allow the fourth most points of any team in the NFL. Sure enough, Arizona dominated. The Chargers' defense couldn't get off the field, allowing the Cardinals to dominate the time of possession battle from 37:31 to 22:29. articles.title: Justin Herbert: The NFL's most talented underachiever? Los Angeles Chargers quarterback tipped for greatness but facing more questions
articles.summary: Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh last week suggested Justin Herbert would go down as the greatest quarterback in NFL history by the time he had finished his career - that was followed by a Week One defeat to the Arizona Cardinals as more questions about Herbert were raised
articles.body:
Herbert stepped out at SoFi Stadium as the best player on the field last weekend. He stepped off it having been out-duelled and outplayed by, with the greatest respect to him, everybody's favourite bridge quarterback in veteran Jacoby Brissett and a transitioning Arizona Cardinals team adrift of postseason discussion.

Brissett and a valiant defensive display had guided the Cardinals to a 26-14 opening weekend victory over Herbert's Los Angeles Chargers to pierce, but by no means burst (yet), the bubble of a team billed among the most exciting playoff contenders coming into Week One. Over-billed? Over-hyped? Time will tell.

It was the quintessential Chargers Chargering exhibition based on the discourse of recent years, a disjointed performance of mistakes and miscues negating the influence of superior individual talent. An all too familiar theme to this team.

Now, were you to drop somebody on earth for a day, ask them to watch a showreel of the NFL's starting quarterbacks and point out which they believed might be considered the best, the most feared, the most dangerous, you would bank on an initial eye test leading many to Justin Herbert. He remains something of a dream prototype blessed with the ludicrous arm talent, the marauding ground presence, the dwarfing stature, the fizzing needle-threading velocity and deep ball fireworks - as much, though, fuels most of the frustration surrounding his career thus far.

In his most successful moments, he has been spectacular, a match for any defense in the league and one of the most box office showcases in football. There has rarely been a flicker of doubt over his skillset, but noise-meets-uncertainty over both his killer instinct and credentials among the elite play-callers in the NFL is as loud as ever, you feel.

Herbert finished Sunday's loss 17 of 27 for 209 yards, one touchdown and an ill-informed interception while attacking double coverage downfield with 10 minutes to play and the Chargers trailing by nine. His day had started hot when he led an eight-play, 77-yard scoring drive including three passes for 60 yards to Ladd McConkey, whose exit with a chest injury after his touchdown catch before the end of the third quarter left Herbert and his offense short of answers.

In fact, the Chargers proceeded to go punt, turnover on downs, interception, turnover on downs, turnover on downs on the five possessions spent without McConkey, their offense failing to reach opposition territory in four fourth-quarter drives, while also collecting six of their team's total penalties including five in the second half and three straight on their penultimate series.

The performance came just days after head coach Jim Harbaugh forecast Herbert going down as the best to play his position.

"Allow me to call my shot, like Babe Ruth pointing his bat over to centerfield: Justin Herbert, when it's all said and done, when his career comes to an end, I predict he will be known as the greatest, best ever to play the position of quarterback," Harbaugh said. "When it's all said and done, and his career is finished, we're going to look back and say, 'Yep, that's the best that ever did it.'"

Harbaugh will not and should not change who he is, having become Herbert's most vocal and persistent cheerleader since taking over as head coach in 2024. He has repeatedly hailed his quarterback's potential for greatness and sought to speak Herbert's explosion into existence almost, but with it has come enlarged expectations and a Hollywood fishbowl feel. Is there such a thing as too much hype?

We might add that it is merely Week One, a prime window for premature panic. The Seattle Seahawks and New England Patriots both lost in the first week of last season before going on to reach the Super Bowl, while the widely favoured Los Angeles Rams were just beaten by the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne; nobody wrote them off, nor is anybody writing them off. Seasons aren't defined in Week One, but an unwelcome start has only prompted further question marks.

Part of the intrigue around Herbert this season comes from the hiring of offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, whose wizardry fell flat in a disappointing end to his Miami Dolphins head coaching tenure but has seen his arrival tipped to unlock the best of his quarterback's alien arm. The best of McDaniel's offense in Miami relied on Tua Tagovailoa's quick-release passing concepts, heavy pre-snap motion and a dynamic rushing attack off which his quarterback could tee, so Herbert will be asked to stray from his comfort zone a little. Every quarterback-coordinator marriage needs time to flourish, McDaniel similarly seeking to justify his own advertising as one of the most influential offensive figureheads in modern football.

McDaniel failed to get his running game going at all through second-year back Omarion Hampton, who managed just 43 yards from 12 carries and averaged only 1.5 yards before contact behind an offensive line that surrendered three sacks. It had been an area the Chargers appeared to address efficiently over the last two seasons under Greg Roman, whose run-heavy offense restored some long-lost stability to their attack. No balance, no party.

Herbert was sacked 54 times last season, the second-most in the league, as the Chargers went without two-time Pro Bowl left tackle Rashawn Slater for the entire campaign while losing Pro Bowl right tackle Joe Alt for 11 games through injury. His 225 sacks and 615 hits entering the season marked the most on any quarterback since Herbert was drafted with the sixth overall pick in 2020. Both Slater and Alt returned this weekend, but weaknesses continued to show on the interior of the Chargers' offensive line.

The numbers have often spoken to his ability to join the NFL's premier quarterbacks at the table. Herbert's 24,820 passing yards through his first six seasons are the second most in NFL history behind only Peyton Manning, whom he surpassed for the most completions by a quarterback in his first six seasons.

He also previously began his NFL career by setting the record for most consecutive 4,000-yard passing seasons with three in a row from 2020 to 2022 behind his best offensive arsenal featuring Keenan Allen, Mike Williams and Austin Ekeler. The gradual departure of the aforementioned trio hasn't helped; McConkey, Quentin Johnston and tight end David Njoku are now his most recognised pass-catching targets.

But for all his stats through the air, the one number Chargers fans care about is playoff wins, which currently stands at zero from three postseason appearances. Herbert has fallen in the Wild Card round in three of the last four years, witnessing the Chargers blow a 27-0 lead against the Jacksonville Jaguars in the 2022 playoffs, producing a career-worst 43.8 completion percentage and four interceptions against the Houston Texans in the 2024 playoffs and throwing for just 159 yards and no touchdowns while being sacked six times against the Patriots last season.

There is something to be admired about the ability for Herbert to become one of the prized faces of the league without quite yet managing to break through the glass ceiling. For the purposes of further fuelling an AFC arm's race brimming with quarterback talent, football is urging and willing him on to thrust himself among the perennial frontrunners, and football knows he is capable of doing so.

But games like that of Sunday should not be happening. Year seven is up and running and the Justin Herbert story remains both captivating and impossible to forecast.

articles.title: Former Steelers WR finds new home in AFC West after major injury update
articles.summary: Former Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver and close friend of Aaron Rodgers, Marquez Valdes-Scantling, signed with a new team in the AFC West.
articles.body:
Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season is officially in the books, with one former Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver finding a new home in the AFC West, and he could play a big role following an injury to a team's star wide receiver.

According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler, the Los Angeles Chargers have signed former Steelers wide receiver Marquez Valdes-Scantling to their practice squad. Following injury news regarding Ladd McConkey 's rib, the move actually makes a lot of sense for both Valdes-Scantling and the Chargers.

Valdes-Scantling, who joined Pittsburgh in 2025 in order to play with his former Green Bay Packers teammate turned Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers , showed fans that he still had game-changing speed at 31 years old last season.

Playing for the Green Bay Packers (2018-2021), Kansas City Chiefs (2022-2023), Buffalo Bills (2024), New Orleans Saints (2024), Seattle Seahawks (2025), San Francisco 49ers (2025), Steelers (2025), and Dallas Cowboys (2026), Valdes-Scantling will now join his ninth NFL team with the Chargers.

It remains to be seen if Los Angeles will call up the veteran wide receiver from their practice squad in time for the team's Week 2 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders , but we at Steelers Wire wish Valdes-Scantling the best of luck in this new opportunity.

articles.title: Chiefs reunite with exciting DB prospect after Week 1 win vs. Broncos
articles.summary: The Chiefs signed with DB Melvin Smith Jr. to their practice squad after defeating the Denver Broncos on 'Monday Night Football' in Week 1.
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs signed defensive back Melvin Smith Jr. to their practice squad after defeating the Denver Broncos on 'Monday Night Football' in Week 1.

Smith, a former Southern Arkansas Mulerider, entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent with the Chiefs last year and competed for a spot on the Chiefs' 53-man roster in the 2026 preseason.

A casualty of Kansas City 's roster cuts, Smith was waived by the Chiefs on August 30 before the Tennessee Titans claimed him a day later.

NFL insider Aaron Wilson broke the news of Smith's reunification with Kansas City in a post to his official Twitter account:

Given that the Chiefs are already dealing with injuries in their defensive backfield — namely to rookie Mansoor Delane and veteran Chamarri Conner — fans in Western Missouri should expect Smith to contend for elevation from Kansas City's practice squad at some point during the team's 2026 regular-season campaign.
